decisions.issues: Minor only. Padmini places the bundle into Nagoji's raised hand instead of tossing it into his lap, but the hand-over still reads. The sky is bright with white cloud, not a heavy bank building in the north. Nagoji has faint jaw shading and a small shadow under the lower lip. At reading size the chin reads clean-shaven. The grey at his temple is a broad streak. Padmini's grey threading is moderate, which the ch16-27 bible row allows. Everything else matches: flush gold ear stud, topknot, plain white mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain, ivory conch-marked knife, sound hands, and clear sky at the upper centre for Padmini's balloon.

The rim of the silver chain medallion carries a ring of tiny coin-legend-like marks. At reading size they look like a notched border, and the upper-left caption should sit over the upper chest to cover the medallion (about x 0.24-0.35, y 0.13-0.20). The courtyard paving behind him is rain-wet with puddles while panel 1.2 shows dry ground. The chain is heavier and chunkier than the finer chain in 1.2. Otherwise the beat is right: close on the hands opening the cloth, grey-black dust sifting onto the white mundu, ridged discoloured nails, the pale ridged brand and long white scar on the left forearm, the ivory conch knife at the waist, and sound hands. Clear space for both captions: the upper chest band and the lower-left white mundu.

Clean. One figure: present-day Nagoji seen from behind at the right edge, with a high Kerala topknot, grey at the temples (a little more than 'first grey' but acceptable), a white shoulder cloth on a bare shoulder and a flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging. The Chapter 3 storm bleeds in as a ragged-edged stain, showing the heeled hull, boiling black water, a taut rope across the deck and the flooded square hatch. The courtyard survives at the edges: jackfruit tree, red-tile roofs and stone steps. There is no text and no painted boxes. The dark, low-detail storm sky in the upper-left quarter is the space for both captions. No face is visible (back of head only), so faces is empty. The courtyard floor is drawn wet while panel 3.1 is drier, which is a minor point.

Only v02 is listed. Its composition is right: a tight insert of Nagoji's right hand, the thumb pressed on the folded letter, a ridged nail catching the light, the letter on his white mundu in his lap, and dappled stone above as caption space. But the letter is covered in crisp, distinct pseudo-letters that look like Latin cursive (shapes like 'B', 'a', 'n', 's', '?', dotted lines). That is painted pseudo-text, and it is anachronistic for a Marathi letter. It also clashes with panel 3.1, where the same letter's marks are soft blurred smears. The writing fills the right half of the paper beside the thumb, so a caption placed in the clear space would not hide it.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, lighting and anatomy: a tight insert of Nagoji's right hand, the thumb pressed flat on the folded letter with a pale knuckle and a ridged nail catching the light, the other fingers curled under the paper, the letter resting on the plain white mundu in his lap, and dappled grey stone and cloth across the top fifth as clear space for two captions. Change only the paper. Draw NO letterforms of any kind on it: no alphabet-like glyphs, no cursive words, no dots, no question marks, no numerals. Turn the written side of the folded sheet face-down, so the viewer sees the plain back of the paper. Through it, only a few faint, out-of-focus grey-brown horizontal smudges of ink bleed through, soft and blurred like smeared tear-stained ink. They must match the blurred marks on the letter in the previous panel and contain no individual characters. Everything else stays exactly as it is.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Padmini's hair carries somewhat more grey streaking on top than the bible's 'light grey threading', though it is still mostly black and coiled at the nape, and it matches 4.1 and 4.3 closely enough. Everything else checks out. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a flush gold ear stud, a plain white mundu with no border, the shoulder cloth, the silver chain, the ivory-handled knife and the pale scar on his inner left forearm. Padmini stands with her stick planted and looks down at him. The setting matches the neighbouring panels: the same courtyard, jackfruit tree, stone platform and kalari pit, in afternoon light. Acceptable insert with continuity flaws. The ivory hilt shows the conch clearly, with no text or gore. Clear wall and dark doorway space on the right takes three balloons. Nagoji's head is off the top edge.

Minor only. It is a true over-the-shoulder shot: the right hand moves a reed pen across a sheet of wavy, unreadable ink lines on a low wooden board on a woven mat. Clean. Tight insert of the finished sheet on the low wooden writing board, reed pen laid across the brass inkpot, small brass oil lamp with its flame shrunk to a bead. The sheet carries only abstract wavy ink lines with no letterforms, matching the ink-marks sheet of 10.4. The dark laterite wall across the upper half leaves ample space for both captions. The lamp is cropped slightly at the right edge, which is acceptable.

Acceptable with minor notes. The over-the-shoulder framing onto Nagoji's face in low gold light is correct, and the gatehouse, laterite wall, niche lamps and sunset match 11.3 and 11.5. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch19 row: thick curled moustache, smooth clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud on the lobe, topknot with grey at the temples, shoulder cloth, silver chain, and the ivory conch-marked knife at his waist. Padmini is seen from behind with her stick, gold ear stud, cream gold-bordered sari and no blouse. The staging partly inverts the beat: Nagoji's body is turned toward the market road (shown at the right with an ox cart) and he looks back over his shoulder with a sidelong glance, rather than facing Padmini and glancing down the road. The road still reads clearly behind him. Padmini's hair shows somewhat more silver threading than in 11.5. Lettering: Padmini's balloon can sit on the roof tiles at the top centre-left (x 0.30 to 0.70, y 0 to 0.12) and Nagoji's in the clear sky at the upper right (x 0.75 to 1.0, y 0.05 to 0.38). Padmini's face is not visible, so her tail point is the near side of her head.

Minor only. The chain is a plain silver link chain, heavier than the thinner chain in 12.3. The brand is a pale puckered patch with no letters, and the long white scar runs up the LEFT forearm as required. Dusk light shows in the upper-right corner. The caption fits upper right, over the plain shoulder cloth and sky, clear of the hand.

Minor only. The grey at the temple is a broad streak, a little more than 'first grey' but in line with the later-life sheet. The jackfruit tree overhangs him outside the gate, although the setting places it in the inner courtyard. Otherwise clean: topknot, thick curled moustache, smooth clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, silver chain and white shoulder cloth. He faces left toward Padmini, who stands off-panel left as in 12.2. The large dusk sky at upper left has room for both captions and the short balloon.

Minor only. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead sitting just at the lobe, a little rounder than a flush stud, but at print size it reads as a gold dot. Seen from behind, his silver chain shows as a thin beaded strand at the nape. The gatehouse has limewashed pillars, where 12.3 shows laterite pillars with lamp niches. Both are plausible for the same estate, but they don't match exactly. The beat is right: Nagoji, with topknot, white mundu, shoulder cloth and conch knife, follows Padmini through the gate. She has a black nape coil with light grey, a cream gold-bordered sari and her stick. The jackfruit tree stands ahead, and figures are lighting lamps along the verandah at dusk. The sky has little room left beside the roof, so the two captions should sit top left over the leaves and sky, or on the plain laterite wall at the right. The tiled roof band also works. Any of these keeps them clear of both heads.
